questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A sphere of mass ' m ' is given some angular velocity about a m horizontal axis through its π centre and gently placed on a plank of mass ' m '. The coefficient of friction between the two is μ. The plank rests on a smooth horizontal surface. The initial acceleration of the plank is
questions.solution: FBD for sphere and block a₁ = fr = μmg, a₂ = fr = μmg m m m m a₁ = μgi^, a₂ = −μgi^ / fr / ⟵a

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A gas can be taken from state A to state B via two different processes, ACB and ADB. When path ACB is used, 60 J of heat flows into the system and 30 J of work is done by the system. If path ADB is used, the work done by the system is 10 J. The heat flow into the system along path ADB is:
questions.solution: From the First Law of Thermodynamics: ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW. For path ACB: 60 J = ΔU + 30 J => ΔU = 30 J. Since internal energy is a state function, ΔU_ADB = ΔU_ACB = 30 J. For path ADB: ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW = 30 J + 10 J = 40 J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The temperature at which a molecule of nitrogen (N₂, molecular weight 28) will have the same root mean square (rms) velocity as a molecule of oxygen (O₂, molecular weight 32) at 127°C is:
questions.solution: The root-mean-square velocity is v_rms = √(3RT/M). Given T_O2 = 127°C = 400 K, M_O2 = 32, and M_N2 = 28. For v_rms(N2) = v_rms(O2): 3R(T_N2)/28 = 3R(400)/32 => T_N2 = (400 × 28)/32 = 350 K.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The potential energy function for the force between two atoms in a diatomic molecule is approximately given by U(x) = (a / x⁸) - (b / x⁴), where a and b are positive constants and x is the interatomic distance in meters. If a = 4 J·m⁸ and b = 20 J·m⁴, find the dissociation energy of the molecule (in Joules).
questions.solution: At equilibrium, dU/dx = 0 => -8a/x⁹ + 4b/x⁵ = 0 => x⁴ = 2a/b = (2 × 4)/20 = 8/20 = 2/5. Substituting into U(x): U_min = 4/(2/5)² - 20/(2/5) = 4/(4/25) - 20 × (5/2) = 25 - 50 = -25 J. Dissociation energy = U(∞) - U_min = 0 - (-25 J) = 25 J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A point source S is placed at a distance of 15 cm from a converging lens of focal length 10 cm on its principal axis. A diverging mirror of focal length 12 cm is placed to the right of the lens such that the reflected rays retrace their path and a real image is formed at the source itself. The distance between the lens and the mirror is:
questions.solution: For the lens: u = -15 cm, f = +10 cm. Lens formula: 1/v - 1/(-15) = 1/10 => 1/v = 1/10 - 1/15 = 1/30 => v = +30 cm. For rays to retrace their path, they must strike the convex mirror normally, meaning the virtual image lies at the mirror's center of curvature. Radius of curvature R = 2|f| = 2 × 12 = 24 cm. Distance between lens and mirror = v - R = 30 cm - 24 cm = 6 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A block of mass 2 kg is placed on top of an 8 kg block resting on a smooth horizontal floor. The coefficient of friction between the two blocks is 0.2. A horizontal force of 30 N is applied to the 8 kg block. If the 2 kg block is initially at a distance of 2 m from the rear end of the 8 kg block, find the time taken by the 2 kg block to fall off the rear end. (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.solution: Maximum friction f = μ m g = 0.2 × 2 × 10 = 4 N. Acceleration of 2 kg block a₂ = 4/2 = 2 m/s². Acceleration of 8 kg block a₁ = (30 - 4)/8 = 26/8 = 3.25 m/s². Relative acceleration a_rel = a₁ - a₂ = 3.25 - 2 = 1.25 m/s². From s = (1/2) a_rel t²: 2 = (1/2)(1.25) t² => t² = 4/1.25 = 3.2 ≈ 3 => t ≈ √3 s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about an ideal long solenoid:
1. The magnetic field strength depends on the number of turns per unit length.
2. The magnetic field strength depends on the current flowing through the solenoid.
3. The magnetic field strength depends on the diameter of the solenoid.
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution: The magnetic field inside an ideal solenoid is given by B = μ₀ n I, where n is the number of turns per unit length and I is the electric current. It is independent of the solenoid diameter. Therefore, only statements 1 and 2 are correct.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A binary star system consists of two stars A and B orbiting their common center of mass with orbital time periods T_A and T_B, orbital radii R_A and R_B, and masses M_A and M_B respectively. Which of the following relationships is always correct?
questions.option_b: If R_A > R_B, then T_A > T_B
questions.option_c: If M_A > M_B, then T_A > T_B
questions.solution: In a binary star system revolving about their common center of mass, both stars must always remain on opposite sides of the center of mass. Hence their angular velocities are identical: ω_A = ω_B, which means their orbital time periods are equal: T_A = T_B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A cylindrical metallic rod in thermal contact with two heat reservoirs conducts an amount of heat Q in time t. The rod is melted and recast into a uniform rod of half the radius of the original rod. What amount of heat will be conducted by the new rod between the same two reservoirs in the same time t?
questions.solution: Heat conduction rate is Q/t = K A ΔT / L. When the radius is halved (r' = r/2), area becomes A' = A/4. Since volume is conserved (A L = A' L'), the new length is L' = 4L. Thus Q' = K (A/4) ΔT t / (4L) = (1/16) (K A ΔT t / L) = Q / 16.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two coils have a mutual inductance M = 0.005 H. The current in the first coil changes according to i = i_m sin(ωt), where i_m = 10 A and ω = 100π rad/s. The maximum value of the emf induced in the second coil is:
questions.solution: Induced emf ε = |M di/dt| = M i_m ω cos(ωt). The maximum induced emf is ε_max = M i_m ω = 0.005 × 10 × 100π = 5π V.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In a Vernier calliper, each centimeter on the main scale is divided into p equal parts. If q vernier scale divisions coincide with (p - 1) main scale divisions, what will be the least count of the caliper?
questions.solution: 1 MSD = 1/p cm. Since q VSD = (p - 1) MSD (when q = p), 1 VSD = (p - 1)/q MSD. Least Count = 1 MSD - 1 VSD = (1/p)[1 - (p-1)/p] = 1/(p·q) cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In an electromagnetic wave propagating in free space, the root mean square (rms) value of the electric field is E_rms = 6 V/m. The peak value of the magnetic field B₀ is:
questions.solution: Peak electric field E₀ = √2 E_rms = √2 × 6 V/m. The peak magnetic field is B₀ = E₀ / c = (√2 × 6) / (3 × 10⁸) = 2√2 × 10⁻⁸ T ≈ 2.83 × 10⁻⁸ T.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A 6 V DC source is connected across a series combination of a₂ Ω resistor, a₁ Ω resistor, and an ideal diode oriented in forward bias. What is the current flowing through the circuit?
questions.solution: An ideal diode in forward bias conducts with zero resistance (closed switch). Total resistance R = 2 Ω + 1 Ω = 3 Ω. The current I = V / R = 6 V / 3 Ω = 2.0 A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In a Young's double slit experiment with slit separation d and screen distance D, the 5th dark fringe is formed directly opposite to one of the slits. The wavelength of the light used is:
questions.solution: The position opposite one slit is y = d/2. For dark fringes, y = (2n - 1) λD / (2d). For the 5th dark fringe (n = 5): y = 9λD / (2d). Equating gives d/2 = 9λD / (2d) => λ = d² / (9D).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The dimensional formula of the expression ε₀ (dΦ_E / dt), where ε₀ is the permittivity of free space and Φ_E is the electric flux, is:
questions.solution: By Maxwell's equations, i_d = ε₀ (dΦ_E / dt) is the displacement current. Because it has the dimensions of electric current, its dimensional formula is [A] (or [M⁰ L⁰ T⁰ A¹]).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two cyclic thermodynamic processes 1 and 2 are represented on a P-V indicator diagram. If the area enclosed by loop 1 is greater than the area enclosed by loop 2, then the net work done per cycle satisfies:
questions.option_d: Cannot be determined without knowing the working substance
questions.solution: The net work done during any cyclic thermodynamic process equals the area enclosed by the cycle on a P-V diagram. Since Area 1 > Area 2, W₁ > W₂.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A star has a supply of 10⁵⁰ deuterons (²H). It produces energy via fusion where 3 deuterons fuse according to: 3 ²H -> ⁴He + p + n. The masses are m(²H) = 2.014 amu, m(⁴He) = 4.001 amu, m(p) = 1.007 amu, and m(n) = 1.008 amu. If the average power radiated is 10¹⁶ W, the deuteron supply will be exhausted in a time of the order of (Take 1 amu = 931 MeV):
questions.solution: Mass defect Δm = (3 × 2.014) - (4.001 + 1.007 + 1.008) = 6.042 - 6.016 = 0.026 amu. Energy per 3 deuterons = 0.026 × 931 MeV ≈ 24.2 MeV = 3.87 × 10⁻¹² J. Total energy from 10⁵⁰ deuterons = (10⁵⁰ / 3) × 3.87 × 10⁻¹² J ≈ 1.29 × 10³⁸ J. Time t = Total Energy / Power = 1.29 × 10³⁸ J / 10¹⁶ W ≈ 10²² s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A mass M = 0.9 kg attached to a horizontal spring executes simple harmonic motion with amplitude A₁. When the mass passes through its mean position, a smaller mass m = 0.124 kg is gently placed on it and the two masses adhere and continue oscillating with amplitude A₂. If the ratio A₁ / A₂ is expressed as α / (α - 1), then the value of α is:
questions.solution: At mean position, total energy is kinetic: (1/2) k A² = (1/2) M v² => v = A √(k/M). By conservation of linear momentum at the mean position: M v₁ = (M + m) v₂. Thus v₂ = [M / (M + m)] v₁. Now (1/2) k A₂² = (1/2)(M + m) v₂² => A₂ = v₂ √((M + m)/k) = A₁ √(M / (M + m)). Here M = 900 g, M + m = 1024 g. So A₁ / A₂ = √(1024 / 900) = 32 / 30 = 16 / 15. Setting 16/15 = α/(α - 1) gives α = 16.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A parallel plate capacitor is charged by a battery and then disconnected. If the plates of the capacitor are then pulled farther apart using an insulating handle, which of the following statements is true?
questions.option_a: The potential difference across the plates increases
questions.option_b: The charge on the capacitor decreases
questions.option_c: The capacitance of the capacitor increases
questions.option_d: The electric field between the plates decreases
questions.solution: Because the battery is disconnected, the charge Q on the plates remains constant. Capacitance is C = ε₀ A / d; as d increases, C decreases. Since V = Q / C and Q is fixed, the potential difference V increases.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A particle executing simple harmonic motion takes 2 seconds to move from point A to point B where its velocity has the same magnitude and direction. After another 2 seconds, it returns to point B in the reverse direction. The time period of oscillation (in seconds) is:
questions.solution: Since velocities at A and B are equal, A and B are symmetrically situated about the mean position. Time from mean position to B is 1 s. From B to the extreme and back to B takes 2 s, so B to extreme takes 1 s. Thus time from mean to extreme = 1 s + 1 s = 2 s = T/4. Therefore T = 4 × 2 = 8 s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_id: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.unit_name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question_text: A stationary nucleus of mass M decays into two fragments of masses m₁ and m₂ having non-zero velocities. The ratio of their de-Broglie wavelengths λ₁ / λ₂ is:
questions.solution: By conservation of linear momentum, total initial momentum is zero: m₁ v₁ + m₂ v₂ = 0 => |p₁| = |p₂|. Since de-Broglie wavelength λ = h/p, the ratio λ₁ / λ₂ = p₂ / p₁ = 1.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A cylindrical cavity of diameter a exists inside an infinitely long cylinder of diameter 2a carrying a uniform axial current density J. If the magnitude of the magnetic field at a point P on the axis of the cavity is given by (N / 12) μ₀ a J, find the value of integer N.
questions.solution: Using the principle of superposition: B = B_complete - B_cavity. The distance from the cylinder axis to cavity axis is d = a/2. Evaluating Ampere's law at point P yields B = (5/12) μ₀ a J. Therefore, N = 5.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A ball of mass 0.2 kg is projected vertically upwards with an initial speed of 20 m/s. Taking g = 10 m/s² and neglecting air resistance, calculate the maximum gravitational potential energy (in Joules) gained by the ball relative to its release height.
questions.solution: By conservation of mechanical energy, the gain in potential energy equals the initial kinetic energy: ΔU = (1/2) m v² = (1/2) × 0.2 kg × (20 m/s)² = 0.1 × 400 = 40 J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In a series LCR alternating current circuit, the resistance is R = 30 Ω, the inductive reactance is X_L = 80 Ω, and the capacitive reactance is X_C = 40 Ω. Calculate the impedance of the circuit (in Ω).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A 12 V battery of internal resistance 4 Ω is connected to a balanced Wheatstone bridge network whose equivalent external resistance is 2R. In order that maximum power is delivered to the network, find the required value of R (in Ω).
questions.solution: By the Maximum Power Transfer Theorem, power delivered to the external network is maximized when R_ext = r_int. Hence 2R = 4 Ω => R = 2 Ω.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The polymerization of propene to polypropene is represented by n (CH₃-CH=CH₂) -> -(CH(CH₃)-CH₂)ₙ-. The average bond dissociation enthalpy of C=C is 590 kJ/mol and that of C-C is 331 kJ/mol at 298 K. If the total enthalpy of polymerization is -360 kJ/mol, find the value of n.
questions.solution: For each propene monomer, one C=C bond is broken (+590 kJ/mol) and two C-C single bonds are formed (2 × -331 = -662 kJ/mol). Enthalpy change per mole of monomer = 590 - 662 = -72 kJ/mol. For n units, ΔH = n × (-72 kJ/mol) = -360 kJ/mol => n = 5.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: When cis-but-2-ene is treated with cold dilute alkaline KMnO₄ (Baeyer's reagent), the stereochemical product formed is:
questions.option_c: A racemic mixture of (±)-2,3-butanediol formed by anti-addition
questions.option_d: A racemic mixture of (±)-2,3-butanediol formed by syn-addition
questions.solution: Hydroxylation of alkenes using cold alkaline KMnO₄ proceeds via syn-addition. Syn-addition on a cis-alkene yields the meso compound (cis + syn -> meso). Thus, meso-2,3-butanediol is formed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A KMnO₄ solution is standardized by titration against primary standard As₂O₃(s). A 0.1156 g sample of As₂O₃ (molar mass = 198 g/mol) requires 27.08 mL of KMnO₄ solution in acidic medium. The molarity of the KMnO₄ solution is [Atomic mass of As = 75]:
questions.solution: As₂O₃ is oxidized from As(III) to As(V), releasing 4 electrons per mole of As₂O₃ (n-factor = 4). MnO₄⁻ is reduced from Mn(VII) to Mn(II), accepting 5 electrons (n-factor = 5). Equivalents of As₂O₃ = (0.1156 / 198) × 4 = 0.002335 eq. Equivalents of KMnO₄ = M × 5 × (27.08 / 1000) = 0.1354 M. Equating: 0.1354 M = 0.002335 => M = 0.0172 M.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The equivalent conductivity of an N/10 solution of acetic acid at 25°C is 14.3 ohm⁻¹ cm² eq⁻¹. If the limiting equivalent conductivity of acetic acid at infinite dilution is 390.71 ohm⁻¹ cm² eq⁻¹, what is the degree of dissociation of acetic acid?
questions.solution: Degree of dissociation α = Λ_eq / Λ_eq° = 14.3 / 390.71 = 0.0366 = 3.66%.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The sequence of an mRNA molecule transcribed from a DNA template strand with the sequence 5'-AGCTACACT-3' is:
questions.solution: Transcription synthesizes an antiparallel RNA strand complementary to the template. Template 5'-AGCTACACT-3' yields the complementary RNA 3'-UCGAUGUGA-5'. Read in the conventional 5' to 3' direction, the sequence is 5'-AGUGUAGCU-3'.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following diatomic species is NOT paramagnetic (i.e. is diamagnetic)?
questions.solution: According to Molecular Orbital Theory, O₂²⁻ (peroxide ion) has 18 electrons. Its electronic configuration has all electrons completely paired, including filled π*2p orbitals. Hence it has no unpaired electrons and is diamagnetic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements regarding atomic orbitals and quantum wave functions is correct?
1. Ψ² represents the electron probability density.
2. The number of peaks in the radial probability distribution is n - l.
3. A node is a region where the probability of finding the electron is zero.
questions.solution: All three statements are correct: Born's interpretation identifies Ψ² as probability density; radial nodes = n - l - 1 which makes total peaks = n - l; and a node is a region where Ψ = 0 (zero probability density).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Consider the nucleophilic substitution reactions of methyl bromide with hydroxide ion:
(i) CH₃-Br + OH⁻ -> CH₃-OH + Br⁻ in ethanol (EtOH)
(ii) CH₃-Br + OH⁻ -> CH₃-OH + Br⁻ in DMSO
Which statement is correct regarding their reaction rates?
questions.option_a: Reaction (ii) takes place much faster than reaction (i)
questions.option_b: Reaction (i) takes place faster than reaction (ii)
questions.option_c: Both reactions proceed at the exact same rate
questions.option_d: Both reactions proceed via an SN1 pathway
questions.solution: This is a bimolecular nucleophilic substitution (SN2). In protic solvents like EtOH, the nucleophile OH⁻ is strongly solvated via hydrogen bonding, retarding its attack. In polar aprotic solvents like DMSO, anions are poorly solvated and highly nucleophilic, making reaction (ii) much faster.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In a Bohr hydrogen atom, two electrons revolve around the nucleus in circular orbits of radii r and 4r. The ratio of the time periods taken by them to complete one revolution (T₁ : T₂) is:
questions.solution: In Bohr's model, orbital radius r ∝ n² and orbital period T ∝ n³ ∝ r^(3/2). Thus T₁ / T₂ = (r / 4r)^(3/2) = (1/4)^(3/2) = 1/8. The ratio is 1 : 8.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The acid dissociation constants of two weak acids HA₁ and HA₂ are 3.14 × 10⁻⁴ and 1.96 × 10⁻⁵ respectively. The relative acidic strength of the two acids (ratio of degrees of dissociation α₁ / α₂ at identical molar concentrations) is approximately:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
What are the essential conditions for an open-chain organic molecule to exhibit ring-chain isomerism?
i. Minimum number of carbon atoms must be 3
ii. Minimum number of carbon atoms must be 4
iii. At least 1 degree of unsaturation must be present
iv. At least 2 degrees of unsaturation must be present
questions.solution: The smallest cyclic hydrocarbon is cyclopropane (3 carbons), and cyclization of an acyclic alkene requires at least one double bond / 1 degree of unsaturation. Therefore, statements (i) and (iii) are essential conditions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs of chemical structures represents tautomers rather than canonical resonance forms?
questions.solution: Resonance structures involve only redistribution of electrons while nuclei remain fixed in place. The keto-enol forms involve the actual migration of a hydrogen atom (proton transfer), making them distinct chemical isomers (tautomers).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following sets of compounds consists entirely of isostructural species?
questions.solution: All boron trihalides (BF₃, BCl₃, BBr₃) have sp² hybridization with zero lone pairs on the central boron atom, giving a trigonal planar geometry, and are strictly isostructural.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: An organic compound A (C₅H₈) on catalytic hydrogenation gives n-pentane (C₅H₁₂). Compound A on reductive ozonolysis produces methanal (HCHO) and 2-ketopropanal (CH₃COCHO). The compound A is:
questions.solution: Isoprene has structure CH₂=C(CH₃)-CH=CH₂. Ozonolysis of both terminal double bonds yields two moles of methanal (HCHO) and one mole of 2-ketopropanal (CH₃-CO-CHO). Thus compound A is 2-methylbuta-1,3-diene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the reduction reagents for nitrobenzene in List I with the principal products in List II:
List I: (p) Sn / conc. HCl, (q) Zn / NH₄Cl, (r) Methanolic NaOCH₃, (s) Zn / aq. KOH
List II: 1. Hydrazobenzene, 2. Azoxybenzene, 3. Phenylhydroxylamine, 4. Aniline
Select the correct matching code:
questions.solution: Sn/HCl reduces nitrobenzene to aniline (4). Zn/NH₄Cl (neutral medium) gives phenylhydroxylamine (3). Alkaline reduction with methanolic NaOCH₃ produces azoxybenzene (2). Vigorous alkaline reduction with Zn/KOH gives hydrazobenzene (1). Hence (p)-4, (q)-3, (r)-2, (s)-1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A 100 mL solution of 0.1 N HCl was titrated with 0.2 N NaOH. The titration was stopped after adding 30 mL of NaOH. The remaining unneutralized acid was completely neutralized by adding 0.25 N KOH. The volume of KOH required is:
questions.solution: Initial acid equivalents = 100 × 0.1 = 10 meq. Base added = 30 × 0.2 = 6 meq. Remaining acid = 10 - 6 = 4 meq. KOH required: N × V = 4 => 0.25 × V = 4 => V = 16 mL.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following reagents can be used to distinguish acetaldehyde (CH₃CHO) from benzaldehyde (C₆H₅CHO) via the Benzoin condensation?
questions.solution: Aromatic aldehydes like benzaldehyde undergo the Benzoin condensation when heated with ethanolic KCN to form benzoin (C₆H₅-CH(OH)-CO-C₆H₅). Acetaldehyde does not undergo the Benzoin condensation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: What is the predominant ionic species of an amino acid containing one amino group and one carboxylic acid group in an aqueous solution of pH < pKa₁?
questions.option_a: It exists predominantly as a cation (+H₃N-CH(R)-COOH)
questions.option_b: It exists predominantly as an anion (H₂N-CH(R)-COO⁻)
questions.option_c: It exists predominantly as a neutral zwitterion
questions.option_d: It exists as an uncharged non-polar molecule
questions.solution: At pH < pKa₁, the solution is strongly acidic. The carboxylate group is protonated to -COOH and the amino group is protonated to -NH₃⁺, giving a net positive charge (+1, cation).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: When aniline is treated with excess bromine water, it forms 2,4,6-tribromoaniline. Subsequent diazotization followed by reaction with fluoroboric acid (HBF₄) and gentle heating (Balz-Schiemann reaction) yields compound X. Compound X is:
questions.solution: Bromination yields 2,4,6-tribromoaniline. Diazotization converts the -NH₂ group into -N₂⁺ Cl⁻, which with HBF₄ forms diazonium fluoroborate -N₂⁺ BF₄⁻. Heating decomposes this group into -F, yielding 2,4,6-tribromofluorobenzene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: For two elementary reactions A -> B and P -> Q, the Arrhenius pre-exponential factors are A₁ = 10⁸ s⁻¹ and A₂ = 10¹⁰ s⁻¹. The activation energies are E_a1 = 600 cal/mol and E_a2 = 1200 cal/mol. If R = 2 cal/(mol·K), find the temperature at which both rate constants are equal.
questions.solution: Equating k₁ = k₂: A₁ exp(-E_a1 / Rᵀ) = A₂ exp(-E_a2 / Rᵀ) => A₂ / A₁ = exp((E_a2 - E_a1) / Rᵀ) => 10¹⁰ / 10⁸ = 10² = exp(600 / 2T). Taking ln: 2 ln 10 = 2 × 2.303 = 300 / T => T = 300 / (2 × 2.303) = 150 / 2.303 K.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.unit_id: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.unit_name: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question_text: Both Al³⁺ and Mg²⁺ are isoelectronic ions containing 10 electrons. What is the numerical difference in their nuclear charges (Z_Al - Z_Mg)?
questions.solution: Atomic number of Aluminum is Z = 13 (nuclear charge +13). Atomic number of Magnesium is Z = 12 (nuclear charge +12). Difference = 13 - 12 = 1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The vapour pressure of pure benzene at 298 K is 640 mm Hg. A solution containing 2.5 g of a non-volatile solute dissolved in 39 g of benzene (molar mass = 78 g/mol) has a vapour pressure of 600 mm Hg. Find the molar mass of the solute (in g/mol).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: An aromatic compound P (C₇H₆O₂, benzoic acid) reacts with aqueous ammonia and is heated to give compound Q (benzamide). Compound Q reacts with Br₂/KOH (Hoffmann bromamide degradation) to yield compound R (aniline, C₆H₇N). How many hydrogen atoms are present in one molecule of compound R?
questions.solution: Compound R is aniline, C₆H₅NH₂, which has molecular formula C₆H₇N. The number of hydrogen atoms is 7.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Calculate the total degree of unsaturation (index of hydrogen deficiency) for an aromatic compound containing 4 conjugated double bonds and 1 closed ring.
questions.solution: Degree of unsaturation = number of rings + number of π-bonds = 1 (ring) + 4 (double bonds) = 5.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Assuming 100% complete dissociation of sodium chloride (NaCl) in a dilute aqueous solution, calculate the van 't Hoff factor (i) for NaCl.
questions.solution: NaCl dissociates as: NaCl -> Na⁺ + Cl⁻ (producing 2 ions per formula unit). For 100% ionization (α = 1), the van 't Hoff factor is i = 1 + (n - 1)α = 1 + (2 - 1)(1) = 2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: Four non-zero vectors a, b, c, and x satisfy the relation (a · x) b = c + x, where a · b ≠ 1. The vector x expressed in terms of a, b, and c is:
questions.solution: Take dot product with vector a on both sides: (a · x)(a · b) = a · c + a · x => (a · x)(a · b - 1) = a · c => a · x = (a · c) / (a · b - 1). Substitute this into x = (a · x) b - c to get x = [(a · c) b - c (a · b - 1)] / (a · b - 1).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: Let X₁, X₂, ..., Xₙ be in arithmetic progression with common difference d (a two-digit natural number). Let y₁, y₂, ..., yₙ be in geometric progression with common ratio r = 16. The arithmetic mean of {X₁...Xₙ} equals the arithmetic mean of {y₁...yₙ}, both equal to 5. If the arithmetic mean of {X₆...Xₙ₊₅} equals the arithmetic mean of {yₚ₊₁...yₚ₊ₙ}, then the value of d is:
questions.solution: AM(X₆...Xₙ₊₅) = X₆ + ((n-1)/2)d = X₁ + 5d + ((n-1)/2)d = 5 + 5d. In GP, AM(yₚ₊₁...yₚ₊ₙ) = 16^P × AM(y) = 5 × 16^P. Equating: 5 + 5d = 5 × 16^P => 1 + d = 16^P => d = 16^P - 1. Since d is a two-digit natural number, P = 1 gives d = 15.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text:
Given two skew lines with parametric equations:
Line 1: x = 1 + t, y = 1 + 6t, z = 2t
Line 2: x = 1 + 2s, y = 5 + 15s, z = -2 + 6s
The shortest distance between these two lines is:
questions.solution: Line 1 passes through a₁ = (1, 1, 0) with direction b₁ = (1, 6, 2). Line 2 passes through a₂ = (1, 5, -2) with direction b₂ = (2, 15, 6). a₁ - a₂ = (0, -4, 2). Cross product b₁ × b₂ = (6, -2, 3). Magnitude |b₁ × b₂| = √(36 + 4 + 9) = 7. Dot product (a₁ - a₂) · (b₁ × b₂) = 0(6) + (-4)(-2) + 2(3) = 14. Shortest distance d = |14| / 7 = 2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: A perpendicular is drawn from the point P(2, 4, -1) to the line (x + 5)/1 = (y + 3)/4 = (z - 6)/(-9). The equation of the perpendicular line from P to the given line is:
questions.solution: Let a general point on the given line be N(λ - 5, 4λ - 3, -9λ + 6). Direction ratios of PN are (λ - 7, 4λ - 7, -9λ + 7). Since PN is perpendicular to the line: 1(λ - 7) + 4(4λ - 7) - 9(-9λ + 7) = 0 => 98λ - 98 = 0 => λ = 1. Thus N = (-4, 1, -3). Vector PN = (-6, -3, -2) ~ (3, 6, 2). The equation of line through P is (x - 2)/3 = (y - 4)/6 = (z + 1)/2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: Let P(1, 0) and Q(-1, 0) be two fixed points and R(x, y) be a variable point on one side of line PQ such that ∠RPQ - ∠RQP = 45°. The locus of point R is given by the equation:
questions.solution: Let ∠RPQ = θ and ∠RQP = φ. The slope of PR gives tan θ = y / (1 - x), and slope of QR gives tan φ = y / (x + 1). Given tan(θ - φ) = tan 45° = 1. Expanding (tan θ - tan φ) / (1 + tan θ tan φ) = 1 and simplifying the rational expression leads directly to y² - x² - 2xy + 1 = 0.

Evaluate the value of the 3×3 determinant Δ:
| √13 + 3, 2√5, 5 |
| √15 + √26, 5, √10 |
| 3 + √65, √15, 5 |
questions.solution: Factoring out √5 from column 2 and √5 from column 3, and applying standard row/column operations reduces the determinant to 5√3 (√6 - 5).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: Evaluate the right-hand limit: L = lim_{x -> 0⁺} [ x^x · cos(x·sin x + 1) ] / [ cos(tan x - x) · cos({x + 1} - x) ], where {·} denotes the fractional part function.
questions.solution: As x -> 0⁺: lim x^x = 1. Inside the numerator cosine: x·sin x + 1 -> 1, so the numerator approaches 1 · cos(1) = cos(1). In the denominator: tan x - x -> 0, so cos(tan x - x) -> cos(0) = 1. For small positive x, {x + 1} = x, so {x + 1} - x = 0, giving cos(0) = 1. Therefore L = cos(1) / (1 · 1) = cos(1).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: Which of the following vector identities is identically true for any 3D vector a = a_x i + a_y j + a_z k?
questions.option_b: If |a| = |b| = |a - b| = 1, then the angle between a and b is π/2
questions.option_c: (a + b) is always orthogonal to (a - b)
questions.option_d: a × b = b × a for all vectors a, b
questions.solution: By definition of Cartesian components, a · i = a_x, a · j = a_y, and a · k = a_z. Therefore, (a · i)² + (a · j)² + (a · k)² = a_x² + a_y² + a_z² = |a|².

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: If α, β, and γ are the number of elements in finite sets A, B, and C respectively, and the sum of the number of all subsets of A, B, and C is 28, find the maximum number of ordered triplets (α, β, γ) that can be formed.
questions.solution: The number of subsets of a set of n elements is 2ⁿ. Thus 2^α + 2^β + 2^γ = 28. Writing 28 as a sum of three powers of 2: 28 = 16 + 8 + 4 = 2⁴ + 2³ + 2². The values {α, β, γ} must be the distinct set {4, 3, 2}. The number of ordered permutations of 3 distinct elements is 3! = 6.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: If y(x) = ∑_{k=1}^{2n} tan⁻¹( 1 / (x² + (2k-1)x + (k² - k + 1)) ) for x ≥ 0, then the value of y(0) is:
questions.solution: At x = 0, the general term is tan⁻¹[ 1 / (1 + k(k-1)) ] = tan⁻¹[ (k - (k-1)) / (1 + k(k-1)) ] = tan⁻¹(k) - tan⁻¹(k-1). The sum telescopes: y(0) = ∑_{k=1}^{2n} [tan⁻¹(k) - tan⁻¹(k-1)] = tan⁻¹(2n) - tan⁻¹(0) = tan⁻¹(2n).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: The area bounded by the curve y = f(x), the x-axis, and lines x = 1 and x = 4 is 12 square units, where f(x) is a continuous, strictly increasing bijective function with f(1) = 3 and f(4) = 8. The area bounded by the inverse function y = f⁻¹(x), the x-axis, and lines x = 3 and x = 8 is:
questions.solution: Using the integration of inverse functions identity: ∫₁⁴ f(x) dx + ∫₃⁸ f⁻¹(y) dy = 4 · f(4) - 1 · f(1) = 4 · 8 - 1 · 3 = 32 - 3 = 29. Given that ∫₁⁴ f(x) dx = 12, the required area is 29 - 12 = 17.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: For a positive integer m, if lim_{x -> ∞} [ x³ ln(1 + 1/x) + x²/2 - x² ] = 1/m, then the value of m is:
questions.solution: Using Taylor series expansion ln(1 + t) = t - t²/2 + t³/3 - ... where t = 1/x: x³ [1/x - 1/(2x²) + 1/(3x³) - ...] = x² - x/2 + 1/3 - ... Evaluating the limit gives 1/3. Hence 1/m = 1/3 => m = 3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: The general solution to the first-order differential equation dy/dx = y f'(x) - y² f(x), where f(x) is a given differentiable non-zero function, is:
questions.solution: This is a Bernoulli equation. Divide by y²: y⁻² dy/dx - y⁻¹ f'(x) = -f(x). Substitute z = y⁻¹ => dz/dx = -y⁻² dy/dx. This yields dz/dx + f'(x) z = f(x). The integrating factor is e^{∫ f'(x) dx} = f(x). Then d/dx [z f(x)] = f(x). Integrating gives z f(x) = x + C => f(x) / y = x + C => f(x) = y (x + C).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: Let f(x) be an infinitely differentiable function on R satisfying f(2x² - 1) = 2x³ f(x) for all x ∈ R. Then the 2010th derivative evaluated at x = 0, f⁽²⁰¹⁰⁾(0), is:
questions.solution: Substitute -x for x: f(2(-x)² - 1) = 2(-x)³ f(-x) => f(2x² - 1) = -2x³ f(-x). Since f(2x² - 1) = 2x³ f(x), it follows that f(-x) = -f(x), meaning f(x) is an odd function. Any even-order derivative of an odd function is itself an odd function. Since 2010 is an even number, f⁽²⁰¹⁰⁾(x) is an odd function, so f⁽²⁰¹⁰⁾(0) = 0.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: If the cubic equation in 11^x given by 2 · (11^x)³ - 8 · (11^x)² + 16 · (11^x) - 4 = 0 has three real roots x₁, x₂, x₃, then the product of the transformed roots (11^x₁)(11^x₂)(11^x₃) = 11^(x₁ + x₂ + x₃) is equal to:
questions.solution: Let t = 11^x. The equation is 2t³ - 8t² + 16t - 4 = 0. By Vieta's formulas, product of roots t₁ t₂ t₃ = -(-4)/2 = 2. Since t = 11^x, (11^x₁)(11^x₂)(11^x₃) = 11^(x₁ + x₂ + x₃) = 2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: Let f : [-1, 1] -> R be a strictly monotonic one-to-one function. The number of real solutions to the equation f(x³ + 14x² + 13x - 5) = f(1 - x² + x³) is:
questions.solution: Since f is one-to-one, f(u) = f(v) implies u = v. Thus x³ + 14x² + 13x - 5 = 1 - x² + x³ => 15x² + 13x - 6 = 0 => (3x - 1)(5x + 6) = 0 => x = 1/3 or x = -6/5 = -1.2. Since the domain is [-1, 1], x = -1.2 is invalid. Thus only x = 1/3 is a solution, giving exactly 1 real solution.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: Consider the differential equation dy/dx = e^(2x) with initial condition y(0) = 1. If 2y f(x) = m e^(2x) + n, evaluate (m + n) f(0).
questions.solution: Integrating dy = e^(2x) dx yields y = (1/2) e^(2x) + C. With y(0) = 1: 1 = 1/2 + C => C = 1/2. Thus 2y = e^(2x) + 1. Here m = 1, n = 1, f(x) = 1 => (m + n) f(0) = (1 + 1)(1) = 2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: A security locker can be opened by dialing a unique 3-digit secret code (from 000 to 999). A person who does not know the code tries dialing distinct combinations at random without replacement. If the probability of opening the locker on any specific k-th trial is p, calculate the value of 1000 · p.
questions.solution: There are 1000 total equiprobable 3-digit codes. When sampling without replacement, the probability that the correct code is chosen on the k-th trial is p = 1 / 1000 = 0.001. Therefore 1000 · p = 1000 × 0.001 = 1.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: If the indefinite integral ∫ (1 - 2019 cos² x) / [(sin x)²⁰¹⁹ cos² x] dx = tan x · f(x) + C, evaluate the numerical value of f(π/2).
questions.solution: Rewrite the integral: ∫ sec² x / (sin x)²⁰¹⁹ dx - 2019 ∫ cosec²⁰¹⁹ x dx. Using integration by parts on the first term yields tan x · (sin x)⁻²⁰¹⁹ + C. Therefore f(x) = 1 / (sin x)²⁰¹⁹. Since sin(π/2) = 1, f(π/2) = 1 / 1²⁰¹⁹ = 1.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: For the five observations {2, 4, 6, 8, 10} with mean equal to 6, calculate the population variance σ² = (1/N) ∑ (x_i - μ)².
questions.solution: Deviations from mean 6 are (2-6) = -4, (4-6) = -2, (6-6) = 0, (8-6) = 2, (10-6) = 4. Squared deviations: 16, 4, 0, 4, 16. Sum = 40. Population variance σ² = 40 / 5 = 8.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: A point (x, y) is selected uniformly at random from the unit square [0, 1] × [0, 1]. Let event A be defined by y² > x and event B be defined by x² > y. Find the probability P(A ∩ B).
questions.solution: If y² > x and x² > y for points in [0, 1] × [0, 1], then y⁴ > x² > y => y(y³ - 1) > 0. For y ∈ [0, 1], y(y³ - 1) ≤ 0, which cannot be strictly positive. Thus the intersection region A ∩ B is empty (measure zero), so P(A ∩ B) = 0.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: Let a₁, a₂, ..., aₙ be positive real numbers with a₁ = 0 satisfying the relation aᵢ² = a_{i-1}² + 2 a_{i-1} + 1 for all i ≥ 2. Find the value of a₂.
questions.solution: For i = 2: a₂² = a₁² + 2 a₁ + 1. Since a₁ = 0, a₂² = 0 + 0 + 1 = 1 => a₂ = 1.
